newsitem.title: KENYA: Aid agencies cross into eastern Zaire, U.N..
newsitem.headline: Aid agencies cross into eastern Zaire, U.N..

text.p: A U.N. aid assessment team and a group of non-U.N. aid agencies crossed the border from Rwanda to the eastern Zairean city of Goma on Monday, U.N. officials said.
The U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs (DHA) said a U.N. aid assessment team and vehicles and staff from the agencies crossed by road to Goma from the Rwandan border town of Gisenyi.
DHA officials in Nairobi said a second U.N. assessment team crossed from Rwanda to the eastern Zairean town of Bukavu.
But a WFP spokeswoman in Nairobi said she was still waiting for confirmation that the U.N. teams had crossed the border because the last she had heard they were involved in paperwork.

Both Goma and Bukavu are held by rebel forces. The Rwandan government on Sunday gave the go ahead for some aid to reach eastern Zaire from its territory but still wants the bulk of aid to come into Rwanda in a bid to coax the refugees to come home.
